sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bressanone manages its centre through a mobility plan, a limited-traffic zone and a municipality that runs all paid parking itself. The council approved the sustainable urban mobility plan on 10 February 2022; it says about half of vehicle traffic entering the city is bound for the old town, and its core measures include a 30 km/h city, fewer cars in the centre and a pedestrian-friendly old town [0]. The ordinance on access to the limited-traffic zone (ZTL) and the pedestrian zone and on parking permits was approved on 30 November 2022; it states that a permit allows parking but does not guarantee a free space [1]. The municipality manages four barrier-controlled facilities (Priel, Rosslauf underground, Parkhaus Brixen and the Mobility Centre) and eight metered lots; the only free lot is Fischzuchtweg, from 06:00 to 22:00 [9].

Tariffs have been moving up. Most metered lots were last set in 2004, and the municipality announced that from 1 July 2026 they would be adjusted, for example to 2.50 euros an hour with a one-hour maximum at Brennerstrasse, Elvaser Strasse and Romstrasse, with the stated aim of raising turnover and pointing drivers to the cheaper barrier car parks [6]. In May 2026 a local report said the 99 spaces in the southern part of Priel were to be aligned with the barrier-controlled northern part, with no subscriptions there because of the lot's high utilisation [7]. The provincial government approved changes to the Südspange bypass on 7 August 2026 and provides 12 million euros for the municipal section, to relieve the centre and Milland of traffic [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main change is the Dantestrasse garage. It was built in 1993 by Parking Brixen GmbH, later Seeste Bau GmbH, operated for more than 30 years, and passed to the municipality at the end of January 2025 when the concession expired [2]. On 27 February 2026 the city and Seeste Bau settled the court case over the concession: Seeste Bau pays a lump sum for maintenance the city had pre-financed and takes over the cost of structural securing for ten years [3]. On 16 and 17 September 2026 the Parkhaus Brixen system was to be integrated into that of Priel, Rosslauf and the Mobility Centre, with old subscription cards to stop working; we have the advance notice only [8].

For visitors from outside, the Plose cable-car operator describes a valley station 7 km from the town with a large free car park and a bus line [14], and the tourist office tells visitors to allow extra time on market days and at Christmas [15]. We found no source on new garages or on public charging.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Prices are set by the municipality. From 1 January 2026 Parkhaus Brixen charges 2.30 euros an hour by day, and Priel and the Mobility Centre 2.00 euros, with 1.20 euros at night [4]; the underground Rosslauf car park rose to 2.00 euros an hour from 5 December 2025 [5]. Parkhaus Brixen has five levels with 550 spaces and 44 garage boxes and a day ticket of 18 euros [10]; the Mobility Centre has 180 spaces, with park-and-ride users of the Südtirol-Pass paying at most 6 euros a day [11]. Priel is open to short-term parkers only, without weekly or monthly subscriptions, and the page does not mention a live availability display [12].

Our data cover four car parks with 1,130 spaces from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since 27 September 2026: Via Dante (650 in the feed, against 550 spaces plus 44 boxes on the city page), Mobility Centre (199), Rosslauf (191) and Priel (90). Occupancy averaged about 34% on weekdays and 28% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Priel and Rosslauf are the fullest on weekdays at 43% and 41%, and the Mobility Centre reached 99% on a Thursday morning in a single reading; Via Dante averaged 31%. Rosslauf falls from 41% to 22% at weekends, a commuter pattern. This is about three weeks of data and does not include the Christmas market.
